Lighthouse Routes: England and Wales

England and Wales's lighthouses dot a coastline of extraordinary variety — from Cornwall's granite headlands to Northumberland's windswept promontories. Riding to them takes you to the dramatic edges where land meets sea, often via some of the finest coastal roads in Britain.

Cornwall and Devon

  • Lizard Lighthouse: England's most southerly point. The road to Lizard Point passes through the unique serpentine rock landscape of the Lizard peninsula. The lighthouse is now a heritage centre.
  • Trevose Head Lighthouse: Near Padstow on the north Cornish coast. A scenic headland with views along the Camel Estuary.
  • Hartland Point Lighthouse: On one of England's most remote headlands. The road to Hartland is narrow and atmospheric, ending at cliffs battered by Atlantic swells.
  • Start Point Lighthouse, South Devon: A dramatic headland on the South Devon coast with views across Start Bay.

Wales

  • South Stack Lighthouse, Anglesey: Perched on a tiny island off Anglesey's western tip, connected by a bridge across a spectacular chasm. The RSPB reserve here has puffins and choughs. The ride across Anglesey to reach it is pleasant.
  • Strumble Head Lighthouse, Pembrokeshire: On a headland near Fishguard with views to the Preseli Hills. The lane to reach it is narrow and winding — true Welsh single-track.
  • Nash Point Lighthouse, Vale of Glamorgan: On the Glamorgan Heritage Coast with dramatic limestone cliffs.

East Coast

  • Beachy Head Lighthouse, Sussex: The red and white striped lighthouse at the base of England's highest chalk cliffs. Viewed from above (ride to the clifftop car park) or from below at the beach.
  • Spurn Point Lighthouse, Yorkshire: On a narrow sand spit reaching into the Humber Estuary. The ride out to Spurn is unlike anything else in England — a thin strip of land between the sea and the estuary.
  • Bamburgh Lighthouse, Northumberland: In the shadow of Bamburgh Castle with views to the Farne Islands. The Northumberland coastal road to reach it is superb riding.
Many English and Welsh lighthouses are managed by Trinity House, which occasionally opens them for tours. Check their website for open days — climbing to the lamp room of a working lighthouse is a remarkable experience.

Linking Lighthouses into a Tour

A Cornish lighthouse tour (3 days) could link:

  • Day 1: Lizard Point → Pendeen Watch → Trevose Head
  • Day 2: Hartland Point → Lundy Island (visible) → Foreland Point
  • Day 3: Start Point → Berry Head → Portland Bill

Each day follows the coast, visiting 2-3 lighthouses with excellent riding between them. The lighthouses give structure and purpose to what would already be a fantastic coastal ride.

Lighthouses represent centuries of maritime heritage. Riding to them is riding to the stories of shipwrecks, brave keepers, and the eternal relationship between Britain and the sea. keyTakeaways: The route links Trinity House lighthouses from Lizard Point (England's most southerly) to Bamburgh in Northumberland, each reached via first-rate coastal roads.
South Stack on Anglesey sits on an island connected by a bridge across a chasm, with an RSPB reserve for puffins and choughs.
Spurn Point in Yorkshire is unique in England, a thin sand spit between sea and the Humber Estuary.
A three-day Cornish loop can take in Lizard Point, Pendeen Watch, Trevose Head, Hartland Point, Start Point and Portland Bill.
Check the Trinity House website for open days when you can climb to a working lamp room.

faq.q: Can I go inside any of these lighthouses?
faq.a: Many English and Welsh lighthouses are managed by Trinity House, which occasionally opens them for tours. Check their website for open days before you set off. Lizard Lighthouse now runs as a heritage centre, so it is reliably open to visitors. Climbing to the lamp room of a working light is a memorable experience, but access is limited and usually seasonal.

faq.q: Which lighthouse ride is best for a first trip?
faq.a: Cornwall offers the richest cluster within short distances. A single day can link Lizard Point, Trevose Head and Hartland Point, all reached on scenic coastal roads with easy motorcycle parking at the headland car parks. The riding between them is as rewarding as the lighthouses themselves, so you get an outstanding coastal day even if the towers are closed.

faq.q: How difficult is the lane to Strumble Head?
faq.a: The lane to Strumble Head near Fishguard is genuine Welsh single-track, narrow and winding with passing places. Take it slowly, use the passing places for oncoming traffic and watch for gravel on the surface. It is not suited to fast riding, but the reward is a wild headland with views towards the Preseli Hills and, on clear days, across to Ireland.

faq.q: When is the best time to photograph these lighthouses?
faq.a: Early morning and late afternoon give the warmest light and the fewest crowds. South Stack and Beachy Head both photograph well from clifftop viewpoints, while Bamburgh is best framed with the castle behind. Avoid midday in summer when car parks fill and the light flattens. Spring and autumn combine dramatic skies with quieter roads.
